stories.head: QOSMIC raises $3.33 million for optical ground stations
stories.body: QOSMIC has successfully raised $3.33 million to develop optical ground stations aimed at enhancing the orbital data economy. This funding round, backed by Accel and Prosus, highlights the competitive nature of space financing, where even the ground operations are vying for attention. The need for efficient data transmission methods is only set to increase as more satellites populate the skies.
stories.soWhat: If QOSMIC can deliver on this promise, it might just carve out a niche in a crowded market where everyone is selling the same data.

stories.head: Voyager acquires Astrobotic before lunar missions
stories.body: Voyager Technologies has completed its acquisition of Astrobotic Technology, just as Astrobotic prepares to tackle two NASA lunar lander missions. The timing of this acquisition is particularly noteworthy, as it positions Voyager to leverage Astrobotic's capabilities in a high-stakes lunar landscape. With the lunar race heating up, this move could pay dividends if Astrobotic delivers.
stories.soWhat: This acquisition underscores that in space, timing can be as critical as technology; missing the lunar boat could leave Voyager adrift.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has successfully passed its critical design review, a key milestone in its development. While this is a step forward, the actual launch timeline remains uncertain, leaving stakeholders in a state of cautious optimism. The Dream Chaser's versatility could be a significant asset for military applications if it ever gets off the ground.
stories.soWhat: The real question is whether Sierra can turn this review into a launch—because in aerospace, design reviews are just the appetizer.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With a recent $190 million Series C, True Anomaly is poised to make waves in co-orbital security and space domain awareness.

watchlist.title: Reditus Space's reentry vehicle performance
watchlist.body: Having completed its first reentry vehicle, Reditus Space's next steps will be crucial in establishing its reputation in reusable spacecraft.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program may signal increased government reliance on commercial data solutions.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical bid outcomes
watchlist.body: As Anduril and L3Harris team up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, the implications for defense procurement could reshape future contracts.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
